blocks.content: The Cottingham formula expresses the leading contribution of the electromagnetic interaction to the proton- neutron mass difference as an integral over the forward Compton amplitude.

Their paper appeared in 1970, at a time when the origin of the ΔI = 1 mass differ- ences within the isospin multiplets was totally mysterious: evaluations of the Cottingham formula invariably led to the conclusion that the proton should be heavier than the neutron and hence unstable.

Early calculations were consistent with the result obtained from the Cottingham formula, but more recent eval- uations indicate higher values for mQED – we will compare the available results with the outcome of our calculation in Sect.
Walker-Loud et al. [6] performed a new evaluation of the Cottingham formula.

The discovery of QCD and asymptotic freedom led to a fully transparent picture for the properties of the Compton amplitude in the region where both ν and q2 are large and where the divergence of the Cottingham formula arises [14– 17].
Sections 23 and 24 compare the outcome of our analysis with results obtained on the lattice and with other recent evaluations of the Cottingham formula.

blocks.title: Abstract
blocks.content:
The Cottingham formula expresses the leading
contribution of the electromagnetic interaction to the proton-
neutron mass difference as an integral over the forward
Compton amplitude. Since quarks and gluons reggeize, the
dispersive representation of this amplitude requires a sub-
traction. We assume that the asymptotic behaviour is dom-
inated by Reggeon exchange. This leads to a sum rule that
expresses the subtraction function in terms of measurable
quantities. The evaluation of this sum rule leads to m p−n
QED =
0.58 ± 0.16 MeV.

blocks.title: Decomposition of the mass shift
blocks.content:
In the framework of QCD+QED, the mass of a particle
is determined by the bare parameters that occur in the
Lagrangian and the cutoff used to regularize the theory. If
the electromagnetic interaction is turned off, only the QCD
coupling constant, the quark masses and the cutoff are rele-
vant. To order e2, the e.m. interaction changes the mass not
only by the above integral, but in addition by the contribution
ΔmΛ, which arises from the change in the bare parameters
needed for the mass of the particle to stay ﬁnite when the
cutoff Λ is removed – the bare quantities depend on Λ as
well as on e.

Accordingly, the elastic contribution to the Cottingham formula is unambiguous.

The prediction obtained for the difference between the magnetic polar- izability of proton and neutron [11] is in agreement with experiment, but this represents only a rather weak test of Reggeon dominance, because the uncertainties in the experimental result are rather large.
The errors attached to the recent lattice result of [74] are much smaller – it is encouraging that Reggeon dominance passes this more stringent test as well.
With the experimental value of the mass difference, the above result implies that the part due to the difference between mu and md is given by m p−n QCD = −1.87 ∓0.16 MeV.
The evaluations of the Cottingham formula in [6–8] lead to values for mQED around 1 MeV.

On the other hand, quite apart from the sensitivity to the precise form of the assumptions underlying those models, the uncertainties in the result for mQED are much larger than ours, because 123 the experimental determination of β p−n M , which plays a key role in that approach, is subject to large uncertainties.
